_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

You already have **`~/.ssh/id_ed25519`** — that one is almost certainly tied to **swapnilkapoor-ST** (that’s what `ssh -T git@github.com` showed). For **swapnilkapoor22**, use a **second key** and tell SSH to use it only for this repo.

---

### 1. Create a key for swapnilkapoor22

In Terminal:

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "swapnilkapoor22-github" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_swapnilkapoor22
```

When prompted for a passphrase, you can leave it empty or set one (more secure).

---

### 2. Add the **public** key to GitHub (swapnilkapoor22)

1. Copy the public key:
   ```bash
   pbcopy < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_swapnilkapoor22.pub
   ```
2. In the browser, sign in as **swapnilkapoor22** (not swapnilkapoor-ST).
3. Go to **Settings** → **SSH and GPG keys** → **New SSH key**  
   [https://github.com/settings/keys](https://github.com/settings/keys)
4. Title: e.g. `Mac WeSolve`
5. Paste, save.

---

### 3. SSH config (host alias)

Create or edit **`~/.ssh/config`**:

```bash
nano ~/.ssh/config
```

Add:

```sshconfig
# Default GitHub (swapnilkapoor-ST) — optional, only if you still use it
Host github.com
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
  IdentitiesOnly yes

# swapnilkapoor22 repos
Host github.com-swapnilkapoor22
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_swapnilkapoor22
  IdentitiesOnly yes
```

`IdentitiesOnly yes` stops SSH from trying your other key first.

Set permissions:

```bash
chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config
```

---

### 4. Load the key (if you use a passphrase)

```bash
ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_swapnilkapoor22
```

---

### 5. Test as swapnilkapoor22

```bash
ssh -T git@github.com-swapnilkapoor22
```

You should see: `Hi swapnilkapoor22! ...`

(Plain `git@github.com` should still say **swapnilkapoor-ST**.)

---

### 6. Point this repo at that host

```bash
cd /Users/swapnilkapoor/IdeaProjects/spec-driven-development/WeSolve/WeSolve
git remote set-url origin git@github.com-swapnilkapoor22:swapnilkapoor22/WeSolve.git
git push -u origin main
```

The important part: the hostname is **`github.com-swapnilkapoor22`**, not `github.com` — that’s what picks the right key.

---

### If something still fails

| Symptom | Fix |
|--------|-----|
| Still says `swapnilkapoor-ST` | Check `git remote -v` uses `github.com-swapnilkapoor22`; run test in step 5. |
| `Permission denied (publickey)` | Public key not added on **swapnilkapoor22**, or wrong `IdentityFile` in config. |
| Repo empty / rejected for other reasons | Log in as **swapnilkapoor22** and confirm the repo exists and you own it. |

---
